data.Description: Service accounts with SPNs are vulnerable to Kerberoasting. An attacker can request a Kerberos service ticket and attempt to crack the service account password offline.
data.Remediation: Use Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA) or ensure service accounts have strong, randomly generated passwords (>25 characters).

data.Description: User accounts have Kerberos pre-authentication disabled. An attacker can request an AS-REP response for these accounts and attempt to crack the hash offline.
data.Remediation: Enable Kerberos pre-authentication on all user accounts unless there is a specific technical requirement to disable it.

data.Description: Computers are configured with unconstrained delegation. An attacker who compromises these hosts can capture Kerberos tickets for any user who authenticates to them, including Domain Admins.
data.Remediation: Replace unconstrained delegation with resource-based constrained delegation (RBCD) or constrained delegation to limit the attack surface.

data.Description: The Print Spooler service is enabled on Domain Controllers. The PrintNightmare vulnerability (CVE-2021-34527) allows privilege escalation and remote code execution.
data.Remediation: Disable the Print Spooler service on Domain Controllers. Apply Microsoft security patches KB5004945 or later.
